items.title: Q1 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: High Modernism, WWI Trench Poets & The 1930s Auden Generation · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · F. R. Leavis
items.stem: Which among the following is not written by F.R. Leavis?
options: English Literature in Our Time and the University
items.explanation: Culture and Practical Reason (1976) was written by American cultural anthropologist Marshall Sahlins, not by F.R. Leavis. In contrast, Education and the University (1943), English Literature in Our Time and the University (1969), and Revaluation (1936) are all major critical books by F.R. Leavis.

items.title: Q2 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Late Victorian, Aestheticism & Fin-de-Siecle · Unit I: Drama · George Bernard Shaw
items.stem: Which among the following texts is not based on the theme of disability?
options: Gabrielle Zevin's Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
Julia Heaberlin's We are All the Same in the Dark
items.explanation: George Bernard Shaw's play Mrs. Warren's Profession (1893) focuses on the economic factors driving prostitution and women's limited employment choices rather than disability. In contrast, Madeleine Ryan's A Room Called Earth (autism), Gabrielle Zevin's Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow (chronic physical pain and disability), and Julia Heaberlin's We Are All the Same in the Dark (limb amputation) all center on physical or neurodivergent disability.

items.title: Q3 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy
items.stem: Which statement among the following defines Pidgin?
options: Alanguage that is used as a kind of lingua franca among speakers, though it is not a native language of anyone
Alanguage which has large number of varieties and dialects used across the world
African language used by the natives to showcase their culture and customs
language with structured grammar and sound system spoken in Australia
items.explanation: A pidgin is a simplified contact language that develops as a lingua franca among speakers who do not share a common language, typically for trade or basic communication. Unlike a creole, a pidgin has no native speakers and arises out of practical necessity in multicultural contact zones.

items.title: Q4 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: What is the appropriate term for the study of language across time (e.g. the history of the changes in a language)?
items.explanation: Introduced by Ferdinand de Saussure in his Course in General Linguistics (1916), diachronic linguistics studies the historical evolution and changes of a language across time. In contrast, synchronic linguistics analyzes a language system as it exists at a single, specific point in time.

items.title: Q5 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy
items.stem: Which among the following rightly defines'homonyms'?
options: Morphemes which sound different but have the same meanings
Morphemes which sound the same but have different meanings
Morphemes which are added to other morphemes
Morphemes which sound the same but have different spellings
items.explanation: Homonyms are words that share the same pronunciation (and often the same spelling) but possess completely different, unrelated meanings and etymologies, such as 'bank' (a financial institution) and 'bank' (the riverbank).

items.title: Q6 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy
items.stem: What among the following rightly defines Pragmatics?
options: Study of the units of meaning in a language and their pattern of occurrence
The study of meaning in context
items.explanation: Pragmatics is the branch of linguistics that studies how context influences the interpretation of meaning in communication. While semantics examines literal word and sentence meanings in the abstract, pragmatics analyzes speaker intent, implicature, and situational context.

items.title: Q7 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which among the following does not relate to Universal Grammar?
options: It is based on the idea that certain aspects of syntactic structure are universal
It suggests that all languages possess the same set of categories and relations
Universal grammar is a theoretical concept proposed by Edward Sapir
Itis based on the postulate that the human brain contains an innate mental grammar
items.explanation: Universal Grammar is the foundational linguistic theory formulated by Noam Chomsky, not Edward Sapir (who is known for the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis of linguistic relativity). Chomsky proposed that humans are born with an innate language faculty comprising structural principles common to all human languages.

items.title: Q8 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which statement among the following rightly defines 'inversion'?
options: Astructure in which an auxiliary or other verb comes at the end of the sentence
Astructure in which an auxiliary or other verb comes before its subject
Astructure in which an auxiliary may be omitted without affecting the meaning
Astructure in which an auxiliary is considered essential
items.explanation: In English grammar, inversion refers to a sentence structure where the auxiliary verb or main verb precedes the subject instead of following it. This occurs typically in question formation ('Are you ready?') and after negative or restrictive adverbials ('Never have I seen such beauty').

items.title: Q9 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which statement rightly defines split infinitive?
options: Astructure in which an adverb comes between 'to' and the rest of the infinitive
Astructure in which an adjective comes between 'to' and the rest of the infinitive
Astructure in which an adjective comes before bare infinitive
Astructure in which an adverb follows to-infinitive
items.explanation: A split infinitive occurs when an adverb or adverbial phrase is placed between the particle 'to' and the bare infinitive verb, as in the famous phrase 'to boldly go'. Traditional prescriptivists discouraged this construction, though it is widely used in modern English.

items.title: Q10 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy · Ferdinand de Saussure
items.stem: Which statement among the following is not true about Ferdinand de Saussure’s Course in General Linguistics?
options: It discusses the concepts of ‘langue’ and ‘parole’.
‘Langue’ denotes actual oral and written communication by member(s) of a particular speech community.
Saussure advocated a synchronic examination of language.
items.explanation: In Ferdinand de Saussure's Course in General Linguistics (Cours de linguistique générale, 1916), actual individual acts of speech and writing define 'parole', not 'langue'. 'Langue' represents the abstract, shared institutional system of grammatical rules and conventions that makes individual utterances possible.

items.title: Q11 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Arundhati Roy
items.stem: Which of the following texts is not based on transgender issues?
options: Myself Mona Ahmed by Dayanita Singh
The Ministry of Utmost Happiness by Arundhati Roy
The Beast with Nine Billion Feet by Anil Menon
items.explanation: Anil Menon's The Beast with Nine Billion Feet (2009) is a young-adult cyberpunk science fiction novel set in future Pune exploring genetic engineering, not transgender issues. In contrast, Dayanita Singh's Myself Mona Ahmed and Arundhati Roy's The Ministry of Utmost Happiness (featuring the hijra protagonist Anjum) directly focus on transgender and hijra lives.

items.title: Q12 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Ngugi wa Thiong'o
items.stem:
Neo-colonialism is the worst form of imperialism for those who practice i,t means power without responsibilty and for those who suffer from it,

it means explotation without redress." Identfy the author
items.explanation: Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president and a leading Pan-Africanist thinker, famously made this statement in the introduction to his seminal book Neo-Colonialism: The Last Stage of Imperialism (1965). He argued that neocolonialism grants formal political independence while maintaining economic exploitation without accountability.

items.title: Q13 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which among the following statements is not true about NEP-2020?
options: The Policy recommends establishment of Indian Institute of English Literature and Interpretation
Itrecommends high quality programmes and degrees in Translation and Interpretation
Itrecommends establishment of academies for each of the scheduled languages listed in the eighth schedule of the Constitution
Itrecommends that proficiency in Indian languages be included as part of qualification parameters for employment opportunities
items.explanation: India's National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 recommends establishing the Indian Institute of Translation and Interpretation (IITI) to promote Indian languages and cultural heritage, not an 'Indian Institute of English Literature and Interpretation'.

items.title: Q14 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Parallel Modernist Tracks: American Modernism, Harlem Renaissance & Indian Gandhian Era · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Cleanth Brooks
items.stem: Who among the following wrote Art of Rhetoric?
items.explanation: The Arte of Rhetorique (1553) was written by the English humanist scholar and diplomat Sir Thomas Wilson. It is historically celebrated as the first comprehensive, systematic treatise on classical rhetoric and logic composed in the English language.

items.title: Q15 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Philip Sidney
items.stem:
Identity the poet who has said that poetry has fallen from its pedestal as 'the highest estimation of learning... to be the laughingstack of

children'?
items.explanation: In An Apology for Poetry (also published as The Defence of Poesie in 1595), Sir Philip Sidney laments that poetry has fallen from 'the highest estimation of learning' to become 'the laughingstock of children,' prompting him to defend imaginative literature against Puritan attacks.

items.title: Q16 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VII: Cultural Studies
items.stem: What does 'bricolage' mean in the Derridean usage?
options: Borrowing concepts from different sources and reshaping them to suit one's needs
Deconstructing the given concepts to arrive at truth
items.explanation: In 'Structure, Sign, and Play in the Discourse of the Human Sciences' (1966), Jacques Derrida borrows Claude Lévi-Strauss's anthropological concept of 'bricolage' to describe the intellectual practice of using whatever conceptual tools are at hand, adapting inherited terms without endorsing their metaphysical baggage.

items.title: Q17 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII
items.stem: Paul J. Crutzen describes 'Anthropocene' as
options: Decisive human impact upon earth's environment and biosphere
Aporia of grand narratives in the post-globalised world shaping human subjectivities
items.explanation: Nobel laureate atmospheric chemist Paul J. Crutzen popularized the term 'Anthropocene' in 2000 to designate the current geological epoch during which human activity has become the dominant influence on climate, ecosystems, and the Earth's biosphere.

items.title: Q18 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Who among the following is the recipient of Nobel Prize in Literature for the year 2021?
items.explanation: Tanzanian-born British novelist Abdulrazak Gurnah, author of celebrated novels such as Paradise (1994) and By the Sea (2001), was awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize in Literature for his compassionate exploration of the effects of colonialism and the fate of refugees.

items.title: Q19 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Jacques Derrida
items.stem: Who has defined defamiliarization (ostranenie) as an aesthetic technique implying the renewal of perception?
items.explanation: Russian Formalist critic Viktor Shklovsky introduced the concept of defamiliarization (ostranenie) in his landmark 1917 essay 'Art as Technique' ('Art as Device'). He argued that the purpose of art is to make familiar, habitual perceptions strange in order to renew our experience of life.

items.title: Q20 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Jean-Paul Sartre
items.stem: What is the thrust of Jean Paul Sartre's impassioned response to Camus' The Rebel?
options: Renunciation of historical responsibility and commitment
items.explanation: Following Albert Camus's publication of The Rebel (L'Homme révolté, 1951), Jean-Paul Sartre and the editorial board of Les Temps Modernes criticized Camus for abandoning historical engagement and revolutionary political commitment in favor of an abstract, detached moral stance.

items.title: Q21 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · Unit I: Drama · Christopher Marlowe
items.stem:
Name the poet who has composed the following poems:
A"A Hymn to God the Father"

B."Elegy on Mistress Bulstrode"

C."Hymn to God My God, in My Sickness"

D."A Valediction of Weeping"
items.explanation: All four poems—'A Hymn to God the Father,' 'Elegy on Mistress Bulstrode,' 'Hymn to God My God, in My Sickness,' and 'A Valediction: of Weeping'—were composed by the foremost Metaphysical poet and Dean of St. Paul's, John Donne.

items.title: Q22 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit II: Poetry · John Stuart Mill
items.stem: Who among the following coined the term 'Speculative Fiction'?
items.explanation: American science fiction writer Robert A. Heinlein coined and popularized the term 'speculative fiction' in his 1947 essay 'On the Writing of Speculative Fiction' to distinguish thoughtful stories dealing with human possibilities and alternative futures from gadget-heavy space opera.

items.title: Q23 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Caroline & Commonwealth / Puritan Interregnum · Unit II: Poetry · Andrew Marvell
items.stem:
My love is of a birth as rare
As, 'tis, for object, strange and high;
It was begotten by despair
Upon impossibility. (Andrew Marvell)

Name the poem from which these lines have been taken.
items.explanation: These opening lines are from Andrew Marvell's metaphysical poem 'The Definition of Love' ('My love is of a birth as rare / As 'tis for object strange and high; / It was begotten by despair / Upon impossibility'). The poem meditates on the geometric tragedy of two lovers whose perfect minds run parallel forever without ever being allowed to unite.

items.title: Q24 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Mary Shelley
items.stem: Who is the author of the pandemic fiction The Last Man?
items.explanation: The Last Man (1826) is an early post-apocalyptic pandemic novel written by Mary Shelley. Set in the late twenty-first century, it chronicles the gradual extinction of humanity by a relentless global plague through the eyes of the sole survivor, Lionel Verney.

items.title: Q25 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry · Samuel Taylor Coleridge
items.stem: Who has composed "A Red Red Rose"?
items.explanation: 'A Red, Red Rose' is a celebrated 1794 Scots lyric poem and song composed by Robert Burns, Scotland's national bard. The speaker passionately declares his eternal love, comparing his beloved to a fresh rose newly sprung in June and a sweet tune sweetly played.

items.title: Q26 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry · Lord Byron
items.stem: In which year “She Walks in Beauty”, a poem by Lord Byron, was composed?
items.explanation: Lord Byron composed his famous lyric poem 'She Walks in Beauty' on June 12, 1814, after returning from a party where he saw his mourning cousin by marriage, Mrs. Anne Beatrix Wilmot, wearing a dark spangled gown. The poem was published in 1815 as the opening piece in Hebrew Melodies.

items.title: Q27 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Jacobean Period · Unit II: Poetry · William Shakespeare
items.stem: Who composed the poem "The Phoenix and the Turtle"?
items.explanation: 'The Phoenix and the Turtle' is an enigmatic allegorical poem by William Shakespeare, first published in 1601 in Robert Chester's collection Love's Martyr. It commemorates the mystical spiritual union and mutual demise of the mythical phoenix and the devoted turtle-dove.

items.title: Q28 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Age of Johnson, Sensibility & Pre-Romantic Transition · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Mary Wollstonecraft, Thomas Paine
items.stem: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman was written by Mary Wollstonecraft. Who wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Man?
items.explanation: Thomas Paine famously wrote Rights of Man (1791) in response to Edmund Burke's Reflections on the Revolution in France, defending republicanism and popular revolution. While Mary Wollstonecraft composed A Vindication of the Rights of Men (1790), Paine's defense of human rights in the same controversy is the text intended here among the choices.

items.title: Q29 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Northrop Frye, Margaret Atwood
items.stem: Who said about Northrop Frye that he did not lock literature into an ivory tower; instead he emphasized its centrality to the development of a civilized humane society?
items.explanation: Canadian author Margaret Atwood, who was taught by Northrop Frye at Victoria College in the University of Toronto, remarked that Frye never locked literature into an ivory tower, but instead affirmed its indispensable place in human social life and democratic culture.

items.title: Q30 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which of the following is not included in the positive evils of Scott as a novelist?
options: His great haste in the composition of his stories
His haphazard financial methods which tended to over production
Haste in the construction of his plots
He had sensitive ear for rhythm and melody
items.explanation: Sir Walter Scott's contemporary and later critics censured him for hasty composition, careless plotting, and excessive commercial output ('positive evils' of his novel-writing), whereas possessing a sensitive ear for rhythm and melody is an artistic virtue of his poetry and style rather than a flaw.

items.title: Q31 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: According to Lev Manovich, "Cultural analytics" refers to
options: The study of culture to decipher the prevalent power relation in the society
The use of computational methods to examine contemporary digital media
Schizoanalysis of culture to locate the contestation among multiple ideological formations
Archeological approach to the study of power and knowledge
items.explanation: Coined by media theorist Lev Manovich in 2005 and detailed in his book Cultural Analytics (2020), cultural analytics describes the use of computational methods, high-performance computing, and visual data analysis to study massive contemporary datasets of digital imagery, media, and culture.

items.title: Q32 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: High Modernism, WWI Trench Poets & The 1930s Auden Generation · Unit II: Poetry · Michel Foucault
items.stem: In Michel Foucault's words, 'Panopticon' refers to
options: The metaphor for the modern disciplinary society
The example of a totalitarian society
The metaphor for a pre-modern society marked by equality
The device for administering corporal punishment
items.explanation: In Discipline and Punish (1975), Michel Foucault adopts Jeremy Bentham's architectural design of the Panopticon as the supreme diagram and metaphor of modern disciplinary power. The constant possibility of being watched induces the inmate to internalize authority and perpetually discipline themselves.

items.title: Q33 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: The goal of Schizoanalysis is
options: To study schizophrenia in the light of neoliberal theories
To reassess the impact of materialist thought in human actions
To analyse the unconscious from a transcendentalist perspective
To scrutinize the specific nature of libidinal investments in the economic and political sphere
items.explanation: Introduced by philosopher Gilles Deleuze and psychoanalyst Félix Guattari in Anti-Oedipus (1972), schizoanalysis replaces traditional Freudian psychoanalysis by exploring how human desire and libidinal energies are directly invested into economic, social, and political systems.

items.title: Q34 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which of the following is not correct about tribal narratives and the writers?
options: Escaping the Land is written by Mamang Dai
Amrutara Sanatana is written by Pratibha Ray
Motherland Being Deserted is written by Salge Hansda
items.explanation: Amrutara Santana (The Sons of the Soil / Dynasty of the Immortals, 1947), a celebrated Odia novel depicting the Kondh tribal community, was written by Gopinath Mohanty, not Pratibha Ray. Escaping the Land is by Mamang Dai and Kocharethi: The Araya Woman is by Narayan.

items.title: Q35 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Jacobean Period · Unit II: Poetry · William Shakespeare
items.stem: 'Alitle learning is a dangerous thing, Drink deep, or taste not the Pierian spring." Which literary critic has expressed the above given thought?
items.explanation: This celebrated heroic couplet—'A little learning is a dang'rous thing; / Drink deep, or taste not the Pierian spring'—is from Alexander Pope's neoclassical verse essay An Essay on Criticism (1711), urging critics to attain deep understanding rather than superficial acquaintance with learning.

items.title: Q36 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Who among the following denounced literary works as the works of devil?
items.explanation: In his Puritan polemical tract The Schoole of Abuse (1579), Stephen Gosson denounced poets, actors, and dramatists as 'caterpillars of a commonwealth,' attacking secular poetry and dramatic performances as immoral instruments of the devil.

items.title: Q37 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Samuel Taylor Coleridge
items.stem:
Who has defined a poet in the following words:

“The poet, described in ideal perfection, brings the whole soul of man into activity, with the subordination of its faculties to each other according to their relative worth and dignity.”
items.explanation: In Chapter XIV of Biographia Literaria (1817), Samuel Taylor Coleridge famously defines the ideal poet as one who 'brings the whole soul of man into activity' through the synthetic and magical power of the secondary Imagination, fusing disparate elements into an organic whole.

items.title: Q38 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: A modem philosophical tendency which stresses the perceiver's role in determining meaning is known as
items.explanation: Founded by Edmund Husserl in the early twentieth century, phenomenology is the philosophical study of structures of consciousness as experienced from the first-person perspective, emphasizing the crucial role of the perceiver in interpreting and constituting meaning.

items.title: Q39 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VII: Cultural Studies
items.stem: Who wrote the book Subculture: The Meaning of Style (1979)?
items.explanation: Subculture: The Meaning of Style (1979) was authored by British cultural theorist Dick Hebdige. Originating from the Birmingham Centre for Contemporary Cultural Studies (CCCS), the book explores how post-war British youth subcultures like punks, mods, and skinheads used style and dress to resist dominant cultural norms.

items.title: Q40 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Bill Ashcroft, Gareth Griffiths, Helen Tiffin
items.stem: The famous text The Empire Writes Back came out in the year:
items.explanation: The Empire Writes Back: Theory and Practice in Post-Colonial Literatures, a landmark foundational text by Australian scholars Bill Ashcroft, Gareth Griffiths, and Helen Tiffin, was published in 1989 by Routledge.

items.title: Q41 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Parallel 19th-C Tracks: American Renaissance, Realism & Early Indian English · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Rudyard Kipling
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true in the context of Rudyard Kipling?

A. Kipling was born on 30 December 1865 in Bombay, India

B. Kipling was awarded Nobel Prize in 1907.

C. The Jungle Books consist of four collections of stories

D. Kipling originally used Shivalik hills as the background of The Jungle Book

E. The Jungle Book was published in 1894

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements B and E are true: Rudyard Kipling was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1907, and The Jungle Book was published in 1894. Statement C is incorrect because there are only two Jungle Book volumes (1894 and 1895), not four; and Statement D is incorrect because Mowgli's stories are set in the Seoni region of Madhya Pradesh rather than the Shivalik hills.

items.title: Q42 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about Ngugi wa Thiong'O's Decolonising the Mind?
A. The complete title of the text is Decolonising the Mind: The Politics of Language in African Literature
B. The text was originally published in 1886 while he was on a short visit to London to attend a conference
C. It discusses that the choice of language and the use to which language is put is central to people’s definition of themselves
D. Through this text the Nigerian author defends the use of English as a tool to progress
E. Ngugi observed that in a school in a colonial setup, the language of his education was no longer the language of his culture

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Statements A, C, and E are true: the full subtitle is 'The Politics of Language in African Literature', the text is dedicated to all who write in African languages, and it discusses how language carries culture. Statement B is false because Decolonising the Mind was published in 1986 (not 1886); and Statement D is false because Ngugi is a Kenyan writer who champions indigenous African languages over English.

items.title: Q43 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true with regard to Postcolonial theory and literature?

A. The Empire Writes Back is a non-fictional text on postcolonialism

B. Black Skin White Masks is a fictional text narrating multidisciplinary analysis of the effects of colonialism on the protagonist

C. A Cntique of Postcolonial Reason is a work written by Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak

D, Edward W. Said wrote his autobiography titled In Place to reflect the love-hate relationship with the West

E. Postcolonialism addresses those questions that emerge in the wake of the departure of colonial masters

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and E are true: Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak authored A Critique of Postcolonial Reason (1999), and postcolonialism critically investigates questions and cultural legacies following the departure of colonial rulers. Statement B is false because Frantz Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks is a non-fictional psychological critique; and Statement D is false because Edward Said's memoir is titled Out of Place (1999), not In Place.

items.title: Q44 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem:
Which among the following is/are not true about Negritude?

A. The movement was started by French speaking African and Caribbean writers living in Paris

B. The movement aimed at examining western values critically and to reassess African culture

C. The movement was against British colonial rule and the policy of colonisation

D. The leading figure of the movement was Leopold Sedar Senghor

E. The movement was influenced by the creed of Art for Art's Sake

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and E are false regarding Négritude: it was founded in Paris by Francophone intellectuals (Aimé Césaire, Léopold Sédar Senghor, and Léon-Gontran Damas) against French colonial assimilation rather than British rule, and it was deeply committed to anti-colonial political resistance rather than an aesthetic 'Art for Art's Sake' doctrine.

items.title: Q45 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Age of Johnson, Sensibility & Pre-Romantic Transition · unit-4-non-fictional-prose · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem:
Which among the following are not true about Feminist Movement?

'A Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Woman challenges the notion that women exist only to please men.

B. Issue of women's suffrage dominated international feminism for more than fifty years,

C. The Female Eunuch was written and published by an African writer named Sarah Mili.

D. Kate Millet's Sexual Politics broadened the term 'politics' to include all "power-structured relationships

E. The second wave of feminism was led by Generation Xers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and E are false: The Female Eunuch (1970) was written by Australian feminist scholar Germaine Greer (not an African writer named Sarah Mili), and Generation X feminists led third-wave feminism in the 1990s rather than the second-wave feminist movement of the 1960s and 1970s.

items.title: Q46 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)

Harlem Renaissance manifests blossoming of African-American culture. Which among the following are the key features of the movement?

items.explanation: Statements C and E are not true: Sir Philip Sidney actually praises Chaucer's Troilus and Criseyde and Spenser's The Shepheardes Calender, and he refutes rather than defends Plato's banishment of poets from the ideal commonwealth. items.explanation: Statements D and E do not relate: in William Empson's Seven Types of Ambiguity (1930), 'unfortunate confusion' refers to the second type rather than the fifth, and the seventh type marks a fundamental division and contradiction in the author's own mind rather than the reader's. items.stem:
Which of the following assumptions are not true with reference to post-feminism?

B. Adiscourse popularised by the mass media in 1990s reflecting a reaction against the feminist theories of 1970s and 1980s

C. Post-feminism establishes the relevance of fender binary where man is essentially powerful

D, Post-feminism is characterized by emphasis on femininity as well as on 'the career woman'

E. Postfeminist discourse extends into other areas such as eco-feminism and cyberfeminism

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements A and C are false: post-feminism was not founded on postulates laid down by Elaine Showalter (who pioneered second-wave gynocriticism), nor does it endorse a fixed gender binary where men are inherently all-powerful. Instead, post-feminism emerged in the 1990s as a critical reaction to second-wave feminism.

items.title: Q56 · Dec 2023 (Shift 2)

Which of these are true about New Historicism?

A. New Historicists do not use thick descriptions for the examination of cultural production

B. Literary works are not autonomous and timeless

C. History is always narrated. History is a matter of interpretation.

D. All historical analysis is objective

E. History is neither progressive nor linear

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and E are core tenets of New Historicism: history is viewed as a narrated, interpretive construct rather than an objective reality, and historical change is understood as non-linear and non-teleological. Statement A is false because New Historicists famously employ Clifford Geertz's 'thick descriptions,' while Statement D is false because they reject the belief in objective historical analysis.

B. Migrancy can expose the migrants and their children to displacement and fragmentation

C. The dominant narratives of belonging and identity can accommodate those who live in-between

D. Living in-between can be a pleasurable experience

E. Home is a problematic concept

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and D are false: dominant national narratives of identity typically fail to accommodate individuals living 'in-between,' and diasporic liminality involves dislocation, alienation, and cultural anxiety rather than unproblematic pleasure. In contrast, diaspora theory affirms that migrancy creates new modes of seeing (A), causes fragmentation (B), and complicates the concept of 'home' (E).

D. Sex and Gender can not be treated as two distinct categories

E. One universal feminism will be the remedy to the historical subjugation

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements A and C represent fundamental concerns of feminist literary criticism: analyzing how women are trapped within a male-centered linguistic and symbolic order, and critiquing how literary traditions and societal institutions are entrenched in patriarchal ideology. D. It rejected the distinction between neumenal and phenomenal world

E. It brought immense revival of interest in classical literature and thought

items.explanation: Renaissance humanism was characterized by an anthropocentric (human-centered) philosophy emphasizing human dignity, reason, and worldly affairs (B), along with an unprecedented revival of classical Greek and Roman literature, philosophy, and rhetoric (E).

E. Truth is not provisional

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: In liberal humanism (as summarized by Peter Barry in Beginning Theory), human nature and truth are viewed as timeless and unchanging essences rather than provisional (E), and the critical mind is regarded as an autonomous, objective observer capable of disinterested evaluation (C). Statements B and D reflect post-structuralist critiques that directly oppose liberal humanism.

items.explanation: Introduced by Edward Said in Culture and Imperialism (1993), contrapuntal reading analyzes colonial canonical literature by revealing its imperial political unconscious (B) and demonstrating how texts like Mansfield Park are complicit in justifying overseas imperial ideologies while concealing the perspectives of the colonized (C).

Read the passage and answer the questions given below:

Studies serve for delight, for ornament and for ability. Their chief use for delight is in privateness and retiring; for ornament, is in discourse; and for ability, is in the judgement and disposition of business. For expert man can execute, and perhaps judge of particulars, one by one; but the general counsels, and the plots and marshalling of affairs, come best from those that are learned. To spend too much time in studies is sloth; to use them too much for ornament, is affectation; to make judgement wholly by their rules, is the humour of a scholar. They perfect nature, and are perfected by experience: for natural abilities are like natural plants, that need pruning, by study; and studies themselves do give about them, won by observation. Read not to contradict and confute; not to believe and take for granted; not to find talk and discourse; but to weigh and consider. Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested; that is, some books are to be read only in parts; others to be read, but not curiously; and some few to be read wholly, and with diligence and attention. Some books also may be read by deputy, and extracts made of them by others; but that would be only in less important arguments, and the meaner sort of books, else distilled books are like common distilled water, fleshy things. Reading maketh a full man; conference a ready man; and writing an exact man. And therefore, if a man writes little, he had need have a great memory; if he confers little, he had need have a present wit: and if he reads little, he had need have much cunning, to seem to know that he doth not. Histories make men wise; poets witty; the mathematics subtle; natural philosophy deep; moral grave; logic and rhetoric able to contend.

Why should a man read books?
items.explanation: In 'Of Studies,' Francis Bacon advises that a person should read neither to dispute nor to passively accept ideas, but rather 'to weigh and consider' what is written in order to evaluate thoughts judiciously.

items.stem:
Read the following stanza and answer the questions that follow:

When she rises in the morning
I linger to watch her
She spreads the bath cloth underneath the window
And the sunbeams catch her
Glistening white on the shoulders,
While down her sides the mellow
Golden shadow glows as
She stoops to the sponge, and her swung breasts
Sway like full-blown yellow
Gloire de Dijon roses.
She drips herself with water, and her shoulders
Glisten as silver, they crumble up
Like wet and falling roses, and I listen
For the sluicing of their rain-dishevelled petals.
In the window full of sunlight
Concentrates her golden shadow
Fold on fold, until it glows as
Mellow as the glory roses.

The first two lines of the poem—
options: Act as a framing device for the rest of the poem
Give the setting of the poem
items.explanation: The opening lines ('When she rises in the morning / I linger to watch her') establish the lyric perspective and observer's stance, acting as a framing device for the intimate, sensory scene that follows.
